about.title: 1. Why I Chose to Become a Web Engineer
about.content: What first drew me to web engineering was the process of thinking through a problem and solving it through trial and error. I was also strongly attracted to the fact that I can see what I build on screen right away, and that each improvement is reflected directly in the user experience. In my personal projects, I find it rewarding not just to implement features, but to keep iterating while asking myself, "How can I make this easier to use?" and "Can I make this structure easier to maintain?"

about.title: 2. What I Have Worked On So Far
about.content: I started by learning the fundamentals of web development, and I now focus on frontend development centered on React, Next.js, and TypeScript. In my personal projects, I have gone beyond building screens to implement features with real-world web applications in mind, including API integration, authentication, state management, data fetching, and responsive design. I have also worked on authentication and data management with Firebase, as well as backend development with NestJS, Prisma, and PostgreSQL, studying with the aim of understanding how a web application works as a whole, not just the frontend.

about.title: 3. The Engineer I Aim to Become
about.content: First, as a frontend engineer, I want to strengthen my ability to build UIs that are clear and easy for users to use. From there, I plan to deepen my understanding of backend and databases, with the long-term goal of becoming a full-stack engineer who understands both frontend and backend and can develop with the entire service in mind.
